# Slidetake

> Write in markdown. Present on a spatial canvas. Record without timeline editing. A markdown file becomes a spatial deck you move through like a map; recording with OBS, every slide is a take, so a fumbled line is retaken on the spot, and Slidetake writes the frame-exact ffmpeg cut and the YouTube chapters. For developers and technical educators.

Slidetake runs in the browser at https://slidetake.com, on your own computer with `npx slidetake deck.md`, and inside other sites with `slidetake.js`. It is open source (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/slidetake/slidetake

## Docs

- [Docs](https://slidetake.com/docs.md): the full guide as markdown, itself a Slidetake deck (writing decks, opening and sharing, layouts and keys, presenting, recording, camera directives, review and cut)
- [Showcase](https://slidetake.com/showcase.md): every feature in one deck
- [Features](https://slidetake.com/features.md): every feature and what it's for
- [Privacy](https://slidetake.com/privacy.md): what slidetake.com collects, what stays in the browser, and which services a deck can reach
- [Home deck](https://slidetake.com/home.md): the short introduction shown at https://slidetake.com

## Writing a deck for Slidetake

- Ordinary markdown: every heading is a card; a heading branches off the nearest shallower heading above it.
- reveal.js decks (`---` between slides, `--` for vertical ones) open as they are.
- `<!-- steps -->` reveals what follows it one press at a time (a list item by item; a paragraph, quote, table or diagram as one press) to the end of the card; `<!-- steps: off -->` ends it early, and anything after that shows from the start.
- Recording: ● Record either records in the browser (Chromium: the deck in a 16:9 frame, one file per take, Render joins the picked takes into an MP4, its sound normalized to YouTube's -14 LUFS) or drives OBS (ffmpeg cuts the takes). Either way, every slide is a take and ← retakes it.
- Fenced blocks ```dot, ```d2, ```echarts (JSON options) and ```svg render as diagrams, charts and drawings. A ```svg drawing is inline: use `currentColor` (the text colour) and `var(--text)`, `var(--text-muted)`, `var(--accent)` (in style attributes) so it follows dark and light. Scripts, <style>, links, foreignObject, images and external url() references are removed.
- Images: alone fills the card; beside text makes a split card; a list of images, diagrams or charts is a gallery (a one-at-a-time carousel under <!-- steps -->, as are two or more of them in a row after <!-- steps -->); several in one paragraph a grid. Alt text is the caption.
- A YouTube link alone on a line embeds the video; the next press plays it.
- Every feature in one deck: https://slidetake.com/showcase (source: https://github.com/slidetake/slidetake/blob/main/examples/showcase.md)
- An optional frontmatter block sets deck options: title, brand, duration (e.g. 10m), pip, camera, accent (the deck's colour; Slidetake's own is green).
- `<!-- view: full -->` makes a card a 16:9 frame for a big image, without the camera unless the card asks for it.
- `<!-- camera: full, on -->` inside a slide steps the presenter's camera; `<!-- view: overview -->` pulls back to the map first.

## Writing a good deck (for an AI asked to make one)

- Save it as one markdown file, e.g. `deck.md`, with a frontmatter block: `title`, and `duration` for a timed talk.
- `#` is the title card; each `##` is a section of the talk; `###` cards are the details under a section. Aim for 5–9 sections.
- One idea per card, a few short lines or a short list each; put long explanation in the speaker's words, not on the card.
- Use `<!-- steps -->` for lists the speaker reveals point by point, ```d2 for flows and architecture, ```echarts for numbers, tables for comparisons.
- Images go next to the file and are referenced relatively (`![caption](diagram.png)`); the alt text is the caption.
- To show it: `npx slidetake deck.md` (reloads as the file changes), or paste the markdown into the editor at https://slidetake.com.

## Running it locally

- `npx slidetake deck.md` serves the deck and its folder at http://localhost:4300: relative images work, saving the file reloads the deck, and typing in the browser's editor saves back to the file. Node 20+. `--open` opens the browser, `--port` picks the port.

## Opening a deck

- https://slidetake.com/gh/OWNER/REPO/PATH.md opens a file on GitHub (default branch); /gh/OWNER/REPO@BRANCH/PATH.md another branch.
- https://slidetake.com/gist/ID opens a gist.
- https://slidetake.com/?src=URL opens any markdown URL that allows cross-origin reads.
- https://slidetake.com/share#deflate:DATA opens a deck carried inside the link (deflate-raw, base64url).
- https://slidetake.com/new?template=blank (or talk, recording) opens a starting template.

## Editing

Every deck opened is read-only. Typing in one makes the user's working copy at https://slidetake.com/edit, kept in the browser; Save downloads it as markdown and Share copies a link.
